head: pr17398-r19
report:
Symlink the repo's node_modules into scratch so bare specifiers resolve.

I found one defect that must be fixed before merge. Once `gc --archive` has copied a session, a live session that has moved on can lose files it removed or renamed, and it can stop opening at all.

## Stop treating a live session that moved on as an unfinished restore (P1)

**Files:**
- `packages/coding-agent/src/session/session-archive.ts:1217-1234` (`liveSessionIsComplete`)
- `packages/coding-agent/src/session/session-archive.ts:1257-1283` (`materializeSessionFile`)
- It becomes reachable through the `session-manager.ts` hunk at diff line 4601, where `setSessionFile` now calls `materializeSessionFile` for every session it opens. It also becomes reachable through `cli/gc-settings.ts` and the gc-cli change: `gc --archive` now keeps the live copy, so every archived session has an archive sitting beside a live transcript.

**Mechanism**
1. `materializeSessionFile` gets a live `.jsonl` path and finds `archivedSessionPathForLive` present. It then asks `liveSessionIsComplete`.
2. That check returns `false` as soon as any archived artifact has no live file at the same relative path. It does not care why the file is missing.
3. A live session that carried on after archiving and renamed or deleted an artifact therefore looks like an interrupted restore. The changelog (diff line 21) gives "a renamed child, rewritten tool output" as examples of normal changes that must *not* be read this way.
4. `restoreArchivedSession` → `copyTreeDereferenced` then copies every archived entry back into the live tree:
   - **Resurrection:** a renamed or deleted artifact comes back under its old name. A renamed subagent transcript now exists twice in the live tree.
   - **Refusal:** if any other artifact was also rewritten so the archived bytes are no longer a prefix of the live file, `copyEntryDereferenced` throws "already holds something else". `materializeSessionFile` turns that into an error, and `SessionManager.open` / resume / fork / render / export all fail.
5. The refusal is permanent. Every later open repeats it, because the archive still holds the old name and the live tree never will.
6. The error message is also wrong. It says "Restored the transcript of … to …", but the transcript never left the live tree.

**Trigger**
1. Make a session whose artifact directory holds `a.log` = `"ORIGINAL TOOL OUTPUT"` and `old-name.log`.
2. Age it and run `omp gc --archive --apply` (`coldArchiveAfterDays: 0`). The live copy is kept, as the patch intends.
3. In the live artifact directory, rename `old-name.log` → `new-name.log`.
4. Call `materializeSessionFile(sessionFile)`. `old-name.log` comes back.
5. Repeat on a fresh session, but also rewrite `a.log` to `"REWRITTEN"`, then call `SessionManager.open(sessionFile)`. It throws.

Probe: `scratch/carryon.test.ts`. It uses the real `runGcCommand`, `materializeSessionFile` and `SessionManager.open`, with no mocks.

**Measured**
```
$ cd packages/coding-agent && bun test .../scratch/candidate__pr17398-r19__t3/carryon.test.ts
archive errors: [] archived: 1
archive tree: [ "...0f4b", "...0f4b.jsonl.gz", "...0f4b/a.log", "...0f4b/old-name.log" ]
opened: .../sessions/--work--/2026-01-01T00-00-00-000Z_01a18630-...-029b1eee0f4b.jsonl
live tree after open: [ "a.log", "new-name.log", "old-name.log" ]
...
archive errors: [] archived: 1
SessionManager.open threw: Restored the transcript of ".../archive/sessions/--work--/2026-01-01T00-00-00-000Z_01a18630-...0f4b.jsonl.gz" to .../sessions/--work--/...0f4b.jsonl, but could not restore the artifact tree (subagent transcripts, tool output) at .../archive/sessions/--work--/...0f4b: .../sessions/--work--/...0f4b/a.log already hold…
live tree after open: [ "a.log", "new-name.log" ]
 2 pass
```

**Changelog claims this falsifies**
- Line 21: "does not mistake a session that carried on since it was archived — a renamed child, rewritten tool output — for an interrupted restore".
- Lines 19 and 31 promise that resume works for archived sessions. Here an ordinary live session that `gc --archive` only copied can no longer be resumed or forked.

**Fix direction:** a retained archive beside a live transcript that never left the live tree is not an interrupted restore. The open path needs a positive marker of an unfinished restore, written by the restore and cleared when it completes, instead of guessing from missing files.

## Not reached in the 20 minutes
Several attack classes were not run, so I make no claim about them: fault injection into the `gc-lock.ts` breaker, kill tests on two processes contending for `gc.lock` / the session leases, and the reclaim path in `gc-cli.ts`. `gc-lock.ts` breaks a lock on `processExists(pid)` with no start-time check. That makes PID reuse a permanent block, which is documented. A lock taken in another PID namespace reads as dead. That last point is an unmeasured hypothesis; two containers sharing one agent dir would settle it.

**Verdict:** not safe to merge. Opening any archived-but-kept session that has renamed or deleted an artifact either brings removed files back or fails permanently.
